name: The BOSS Can Count Pairs
description: You are given two arrays $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, both of length $$$n$$$. Your task is to count the number of pairs of integers $$$(i,j)$$$ such that $$$1 \leq i \lt j \leq n$$$ and $$$a_i \cdot a_j = b_i+b_j$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the arrays. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the elements of array $$$a$$$. The third line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_n$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le n$$$) — the elements of array $$$b$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output the number of good pairs.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1830B — The BOSS Can Count Pairs [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
